    Bellare and Rogaway's encryption scheme is IND-CPA (EasyCrypt examples/br93.ec) #

    Bellare and Rogaway, "Random oracles are practical: a paradigm for designing efficient protocols" (1993): enc pk m = (f pk r, H r +^ m) for a one-way trapdoor permutation f and a random oracle H. EC's file, declaration by declaration and script line by line, in its two parts:

    • abstract theory BR93 (lines 1–422; namespace GaudisCrypt.Examples.BR93): correctness, and the reduction Pr[BR93_CPA(A).main : res] - 1/2 ≤ Pr[OW(I(A)).main : res] by three games (the oracle call of the challenge replaced by a sampling, up to the adversary querying r; the one-time pad h +^ m replaced by h; the inverter);
    • the instance on bitstrings (lines 425–659; namespace GaudisCrypt.Examples.BR93Concrete): plaintexts of length k, nonces of length l, ciphertexts r || p, the textbook's CPA, BR, Exp_OW, and Reduction for them from the theory's, cloned as Instance.

    All of EC's lemmas are proven.

    Translation:

    • abstract theory BR93 with its types and operators is class Params (ptxt rand pkey skey); the theory's clone import ROM as H, clone import OW as OW_rand are clones (Lib/EC/ROM.lean, Lib/EC/OW.lean).
    • module type Adv (ARO : POracle) = { proc a1 … proc a2 … } is abbrev Adv := POracle →ₘ AdvProcs; declare module A <: Adv {…}, declare axiom A_a1_ll (O <: POracle {-A}) : islossless O.o => islossless A(O).a1 are declare module and a section variable with the same binder.
    • A module's var x is module_var M.x : T before the module.
    • x \in LRO.m is FMap.dom §LRO.m x; witness is default.
    • The instance: op k, op l, type pkey, skey, op dkeys, f, fi and their axioms are class BR93Concrete.Params (pkey skey); the three clones of BitWord (ptxt, rand, ctxt) are BitWord.word k, BitWord.word l, BitWord.word n; r || p is r ∥ p; EC's Self.I is I, the theory's Instance.I.
    • module A_CPA (A : Adv) (H : POracle) is module A_CPA (A : Adv) using (H : POracle): A a Lean parameter, so that EC's partial application A_CPA(A) is the module A_CPA A.

    Gap list (what keeps the file from reading as EC's):

    • GAP 1: local module Game1 = BR93_CPA(A) with { … } and Game2 = Game1 with { … } (EC's module update) are written out as full modules Game1, Game2 with the parameter A.
    • GAP 2: ={glob Log, glob LRO} in an invariant is ={glob A, Log.qs, LRO.m} (glob M of a concrete module is not a variable list here; glob A is stated, where EC adds it). In pr_Game0_Game1's seq, glob LRO, glob Log is LRO.m, Log.qs.
    • GAP 3: the restriction is {-LRO, -Log, -Game1, -Game2, -OWr}: EC's {-LRO, -Log}, and the section's local modules, which EC keeps apart from A by declaring them after it.
    • GAP 4: 1: by sim on the oracle's judgment is equiv_proc; stmt_inline*; equiv_auto; auto_progress (sim finds no equality set for the cloned oracle), and OW_OWr's by byequiv=> //=; sim is the inverter's call by hand.
    • GAP 5: call (LRO_o_ll _); auto; apply: dptxt_ll for the logged oracle's losslessness is islossless (applying LRO_o_ll does not unify through the clone's accessor).
    • GAP 6: the pure goals after auto=> /> are closed by hand where EC names the pieces with an intro pattern (rename_i, rintro), and EC's smt(@FMap) is smt_close [FMap.mem_set].
    • GAP 7: rewrite (OW_OWr &m (I(A))) needs I(A)'s restriction {-OWr} as an instance, stated by hand (haveI : Module.Declared (Module.app I A) …); EC checks it itself.
    • GAP 8: three lemmas, and the instance's Reduction, need more than the default heartbeats.
    • GAP 9: the section is declare module A <: Adv {…} with glob R with {-R} for {-A} in A_a1_ll, A_a2_ll (notes/SHA3/Exceptions.md, E14), so that the instance can apply Reduction to A_CPA(A): glob A_CPA(A) is known from above only.
    • GAP 10 (instance): EC clones ROM a second time, at the types of the clone inside BR93, and the two bridges keep H.Lazy.LRO.m{1} = LRO.m{2}. Two clones of a theory at the same types and operators are one module here and share its variable: the invariant is ={glob A, LRO.m} (per-clone variables: notes/SHA3/TacticReview.md, last section).
    • GAP 11 (instance): local clone import BR93 as Instance is made before the section, and the restriction of A is {-LRO, -I, -Log, -Game1, -Game2, -OWr}: EC's {-LRO, -I}, and the clone's variables, fresh for A in EC because the clone is made after A is declared. They show in the statement of Reduction.
    • GAP 12 (instance): EC's module QRO inside I is the module I.QRO next to it; EC's procedure alias proc a1 = A(H).a1 in A_CPA is a procedure with one call (one more inline in the first bridge).
    • GAP 13 (instance): apply/(Reduction (A_CPA(A)) _ _ &m) states EC's restriction checks of A_CPA(A) by hand (⟨by fp_finite, by fp_disjoint⟩, Footprint.Restricted.glob_declared A), with the instance Module.ECGlob (A_CPA A) R from fvP_A_CPA; the last goal of the second bridge (EC's by auto) needs the invariant's Log.qs{1} = I.qs{2} rewritten.
    • [Countable rand] is an assumption EC does not state (the samplings into rand).

    class GaudisCrypt.Examples.BR93.Params (ptxt rand pkey skey : outParam Type) :
    Type

    The abstract scenario of EC's abstract theory BR93.

    • add : ptxt → ptxt → ptxt
    • addA (p1 p2 p3 : ptxt) : p1 +^ p2 +^ p3 = p1 +^ (p2 +^ p3)
    • addC (p1 p2 : ptxt) : p1 +^ p2 = p2 +^ p1
    • addKp (p1 p2 : ptxt) : p1 +^ p1 +^ p2 = p2
    • dptxt : SubProbability ptxt
    • dptxt_llfuuni : EC.is_lossless dptxt ∧ EC.is_full dptxt ∧ EC.is_uniform dptxt
    • drand : SubProbability rand
    • drand_lluni : EC.is_lossless drand ∧ EC.is_uniform drand
    • dkeys : SubProbability (pkey × skey)
    • dkeys_llfuni : EC.is_lossless dkeys ∧ EC.is_funiform dkeys
    • f : pkey → rand → rand
    • fi : skey → rand → rand
    • fK (pk : pkey) (sk : skey) (x : rand) : (pk, sk) ∈ dkeys.support → fi sk (f pk x) = x

        @[simp]: applying BR93.dec to the parameters proc dec uses (H) is Module.proc (BR93.dec.procedure.instantiate …) — the procedure with its holes filled by the callees they were made from, each written as it was in the body (with the arguments in place of the module parameters) and turned into a Procedure by Module.Proc.procedure.

                                                                                              Deliberately not @[simp], unlike the other apply_simp lemmas: its right-hand side is the whole body written out, so letting it fire on its own would turn any goal mentioning an instantiated procedure into that body. Inlining a procedure is a step to ask for by name (simp [OWr.main.procedure.apply_simp]).

                                                                                                The body of proc main of module OWr, as a procedure of its own: the one call it makes to a module parameter (I) is its single hole.

                                                                                                A hole stands for a call whose callee is not known here — a module parameter is supplied only when the module is applied — so the body is a ProcedureWithHoles, to be instantiated (see OWr.main.procedure.apply_simp) rather than run. Use OWr.main for this procedure as a module.

                                                                                                  The concrete instance (EC lines 425–659) #

                                                                                                  We now consider a concrete instance:

                                                                                                  • plaintexts are bitstrings of length k > 0,
                                                                                                  • nonces are bitstrings of length l > 0,
                                                                                                  • ciphertexts are bitstrings of length n = k + l.

                                                                                                                                                                        The record of the fields of a module of type AdvProcs: the fields a1, a2, one per moduletype field, each of that field's own module type.

                                                                                                                                                                        AdvProcs.mk turns such a record into a AdvProcs, AdvProcs.structure turns a AdvProcs back into one.
